mission.brief: On fictional elm-02, low free memory triggered an alert. Save the eight data records at the end of memory.txt in memory-report.txt, retaining all seven meminfo fields and the swap interval. Display source and report with cat after writing. Self-review whether this evidence establishes current pressure; do not add an ungraded diagnosis to the factual report.
constraints: SIMULATOR: supplied synthetic snapshots of fictional hosts, not measurements of your computer or VM. No free, vmstat, df, processes, mounts, repairs or cleanup commands are simulated here.

Score checks factual report bytes, reading evidence and preserved sources only. Interpretation, uncertainty and recommended next checks require self-review; 100/100 is NOT proof of diagnostic mastery.

Type help for supported text commands. For this lab's context, worked interpretation and common mistakes, read HELP.txt with cat. This reference is available in both modes; it contains no repair command.

Only declared report files can be written. > truncates before reading; >> appends. Errors do not undo writes. Finish all report writes before reading sources and final reports: any actual write clears earlier reading evidence.

Keep source record spelling, units, order and final LF exactly in reports. Equivalent supported paths and filters count for report construction. Required reading evidence specifically uses cat on each source and final report after the last write; other tools do not satisfy cat inspections. Reasoning is self-reviewed. Reset preserves history.

/home/learner/HELP.txt.content:
SIMULATOR HELP — memory interpretation
Supplied subset of Linux /proc/meminfo; not live output. kB in meminfo represents KiB. MemAvailable is an estimate accounting for reclaimable cache/slab and watermarks; it is not MemFree plus all Cached. Fields overlap and must not be added as independent categories.
Self-review: does 65536 KiB free alone establish pressure? Why retain both swap totals and swap rates?
Model interpretation: about half the 2 GiB is estimated available. Low MemFree alone is insufficient evidence of pressure. Swap occupancy is 65536 KiB (total minus free), but the supplied interval has no swap-in/out. Occupancy can reflect earlier activity; one quiet interval cannot rule out intermittent pressure. Collect repeated samples and application latency/reclaim evidence.
Common mistakes: treating cache as permanently unavailable; equating occupied swap with current thrashing; interpreting si/so as totals; equating MemAvailable with guaranteed capacity.
Automatically checked: unchanged source, exact eight data records and source/report readings. Understanding, subtraction and pressure diagnosis are self-reviewed, not graded. Type help for commands.
Required checked reading actions use cat on each source and final report after the last write. Other text tools may construct reports but do not satisfy these cat actions.

lesson.goal: Distinguish free, available, cache and swap evidence.

steps.explanation: MemAvailable estimates memory for new applications without swapping; Cached is not all memory available. Preserve the swap occupancy AND interval evidence.
